title: Consumer brands increase ad spend despite slower growth as retail media gains ground
gist: Consumer goods brands increased ad spend 36% between 2019 and 2025, outpacing their 29% revenue growth, with trade budgets shifting into measurable retail media channels driving the trend. WARC forecasts global ad spend will reach $1.34tn in 2025, with retail media among the top growth channels.

title: GUEST COMMENT This year should mark the end of Black Friday as we know it
gist: A former Asda pricing lead argues Black Friday has become a margin-destroying industry-wide discount cycle where most deals are no cheaper than at other times of year, and calls for a shift to targeted, loyalty-based promotions instead of broad discounting. The piece proposes brands use the naturally elevated footfall period to reward loyal customers with genuine deals rather than running blanket sales.

title: Ruggable’s new ad spend strategy shifts focus to ShopMy creators
gist: DTC rug brand Ruggable has shifted about 10% of its budget away from Meta performance channels into brand channels like influencers and CTV over the past 18 months, with plans to grow that brand spend by another 15–20% next year. The CMO framed the move as recognizing that the performance-only playbook that built the brand will not sustain its next phase of growth.

title: Social commerce edges past SEO at The Independent for the first time
gist: The Independent's social-commerce revenue narrowly surpassed its SEO-driven commerce revenue for the first time in September, signaling a structural shift in how publishers generate affiliate and commerce income. CEO Christian Broughton argued publishers should build revenue around trusted brands across platforms rather than relying on search traffic.

title: Ruggable’s new ad spend strategy shifts focus to ShopMy creators
gist: Ruggable has moved roughly 10% of its budget from Meta performance channels into brand channels including influencers and CTV over 18 months, with the CMO citing rising ad costs and declining performance as the drivers. The brand plans to increase brand-channel spend by a further 15–20% next year.

title: Target bets on buzzy TikTok brands like Mellow Sleep to revamp its home category
gist: Mellow Sleep, a brand launched in 2025 that became TikTok's top-selling sleep brand and hit $130M in first-year revenue, is making its physical retail debut at 550 Target stores starting October 18 as part of Target's strategy to revamp its home category with emerging social-native brands. The brand is on track for over $300M in sales in its second year.

title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
gist: Cal AI founder Zach Yadegari built a $30M-revenue calorie-tracking app in two years primarily through a scaled influencer strategy that tied payouts to minimum reach thresholds, before the company was acquired by MyFitnessPal in March 2025. He emphasized finding influencers with tight, quantifiable communities and negotiating performance-based rates as the key formula.

title: The holiday playbook: How brands are navigating launches, stock and promotions
gist: Consumer brands heading into the 2025 holiday season are managing launch timing, restock logistics, and promotional strategies with Q4 representing over 50% of annual sales for some. Brands that sold out new product lines at launch are racing to replenish inventory before the peak shopping window.

title: Google’s Universal Cart shopping tool launches in the US
gist: Google has launched Universal Cart in the US, a tool that aggregates saved products from multiple retailers into a single hub within Search and the Gemini app, with price-drop and restock notifications and checkout tied to Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). The move is part of Google's broader push into AI-powered agentic commerce, where AI agents handle parts of the shopping journey on behalf of users.

title: Why Depop is putting music at the center of its marketing, collaborating with Zara Larsson and Olivia Rodrigo
gist: Depop is building its marketing strategy around music, using data showing 56% of its users attend live events to justify artist wardrobe 'shop drops' with names like Olivia Rodrigo and Zara Larsson.

title: Halloween without candy? What shoppers are cutting from budgets this year
gist: Average U.S. Halloween spending is projected to drop 16% to $162 this year, with 80% of consumers planning to shop at all (down from 90%), and nearly two-thirds of those shoppers planning to skip at least one category.

title: Why brands are turning your favorite beauty products into fashion accessories
gist: Brands like Givenchy and Rhode are designing beauty products that double as visible fashion accessories, blurring the line between product utility and wearable branding.

title: Gold is now the top U.S. export
gist: U.S. gold exports have surged to become the country's top export by value since late 2025, with the bulk flowing to Switzerland, Hong Kong (a gateway to China), and the UK. The author speculates this reflects foreign central banks, particularly China, shifting reserves away from U.S. Treasuries and dollars toward gold.

title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
gist: Meta added language to its commercial terms of use that appeared to allow scraping any website linked to a business account for AI training, then removed the provision after public backlash, insisting it reflected no change in actual crawling practices.

title: UK plans to extend VAT liability for marketplaces
gist: The UK government is proposing to make online marketplaces liable for collecting VAT on sales by larger domestic sellers, a measure projected to raise up to £1 billion annually, with proceeds earmarked to fund tax relief for high-street businesses.

title: Nike hired Elliott Hill to fix a couple problems. They keep growing.
gist: Nike's turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill is proving harder than expected, with Jordan Brand, Greater China, and the core sportswear segment all declining double-digits as the company continues restructuring around oversupply, channel reset, and product relevance.

title: Matalan app orders jump 28% as digital investment pays off
gist: Matalan's new native mobile app reached 1.76 million downloads in two months, driving a 28% jump in app orders and a 4.4% conversion rate — above its 3.4% target — with app shoppers spending 14% more per order than website shoppers.

title: The Entertainer and Boodles back 2% online sales levy to slash business rates
gist: Over 200 UK business leaders are calling on the Chancellor to introduce a 2% online sales levy to fund cuts to business rates, arguing the current property-based tax system unfairly burdens physical retailers relative to online commerce.

title: UK profit warnings hit near two-year high as retailers brace for Budget
gist: UK profit warnings hit a near two-year high in Q3, with 65 warnings issued as retailers cite policy uncertainty, rising costs, and weak consumer spending ahead of the autumn Budget.

title: Discounting is ‘a hard drug to come off,’ but retraining customers to shop full price is a must, brand leaders say
gist: Brand leaders are grappling with breaking customers' discount expectations ahead of the holiday season, describing heavy discounting as structurally damaging but difficult to reverse given competition from Amazon and major retailers.

title: Shoppers expect less for more this holiday season. That could mean a sales decline.
gist: Multiple forecasts for the 2026 holiday season are diverging: NRF projects 4.2% growth to ~$1 trillion, while Circana sees a possible 1% decline and Simon-Kucher projects a 5.5% drop, with 77% of consumers saying inflation has changed their shopping behavior and only 22% trusting advertised discounts. Shoppers are starting earlier, spreading spend across October events, and becoming more deliberate about where they spend.

title: NRF forecasts 4.2% holiday sales growth, muted seasonal hiring
gist: NRF forecasts 4.2% holiday retail sales growth to ~$1 trillion for November–December 2026, but notes that inflation accounts for a meaningful portion of nominal gains and last year's forecast was missed. Seasonal hiring is projected at 325,000–375,000 positions, reflecting a cautious 'low hire, low fire' labor environment.

title: Nearly 30% of holiday budgets expected to be spent by the end of October
gist: Deloitte's 2026 holiday survey finds 28% of shoppers' budgets will be spent by end of October — the highest in six years — with 42% planning to shop October sales events and 1 in 4 having already bought holiday gifts during June promotions. The traditional Black Friday/Cyber Monday concentration is continuing to erode.

title: ChatGPT takes on fashion’s fitting rooms as OpenAI makes major play for shoppers
gist: OpenAI has added a virtual try-on feature to ChatGPT's shopping results, letting users upload a photo to see how products look on them, alongside a Favorites tool to save and organize potential purchases — all without leaving ChatGPT. The move puts OpenAI in direct competition with Google, which launched similar try-on tech in the UK in December 2025, as both platforms deepen their role in the online shopping journey.

title: Why retailers are turning to Klarna as shoppers feel the squeeze
gist: Major UK retailers including M&S, John Lewis, and Boots have adopted Klarna's BNPL service as consumer budgets remain under pressure, with BNPL expanding beyond e-commerce into physical stores via QR-code checkout. The trend reflects BNPL shifting from a differentiator to a standard checkout expectation, particularly among Gen Z and Millennial shoppers.

title: Dick’s Sporting Goods’ seasonal hiring slips
gist: Dick's Sporting Goods plans to hire over 11,000 seasonal workers for holiday 2026, about 20% fewer than last year, in line with a broader industry trend of more conservative seasonal hiring. The company also lowered its full-year outlook for its recently acquired Foot Locker brand, projecting an operating loss of $40M–$80M against previous profit expectations.

title: Walmart opens next-gen California facility to boost West Coast fulfillment
gist: Walmart opened its fifth 'next-generation' fulfillment center in Stockton, California, using automation and machine learning to cut its standard 12-step fulfillment process to five steps and increase daily order capacity. The retailer is also upgrading all 42 U.S. distribution centers with automation as part of a broader supply chain investment.

title: UK plans to extend VAT liability for marketplaces
gist: The UK government is proposing to make online marketplaces liable for collecting VAT on sales by larger domestic sellers, a measure projected to raise up to £1 billion annually. The additional revenue is intended to fund tax relief for high street businesses.

title: Debenhams Group launches faster payment scheme for 30,000 marketplace partners
gist: Debenhams Group has partnered with Storfund to offer its 30,000+ marketplace brand partners daily advance payments of up to 80% of shipped sales revenue, replacing the standard marketplace payment cycle. The service is live across Debenhams, boohoo, and PrettyLittleThing platforms with no subscription or setup fees.

title: Tesco launches 500-screen advertising blitz across Booker’s UK wholesale estate
gist: Booker (owned by Tesco) has rolled out 500+ digital advertising screens across 100 UK wholesale sites in eight weeks, creating a retail media network targeting independent retailers and hospitality buyers at the point of purchase. Tesco's broader retail media operation now has over 7,500 digital screens and reported a 17% increase in active advertisers.

title: Pinterest’s head of beauty reveals the rise of hyper-personalised trends
gist: Pinterest's first Beauty Trend Report, based on search behavior analysis, shows consumers moving away from broad aesthetic searches toward highly specific combinations of color, texture, finish, and occasion — with searches like 'polka-dot cat-eye nails' up 1,585% and 'fragrance wardrobe' up 210%. The platform positions this granularity as a signal of purchase intent that brands and retailers can use for product development and merchandising.

title: Target’s holiday push stresses affordability, exclusives and an AI assistant
gist: Target is launching 8,000+ new holiday gifts (mostly under $20, half exclusive), daily deals from Nov. 1–Dec. 24, and a beta AI assistant called Ask Target to help shoppers build wishlists on its app and site.

title: Walmart enlists Sam’s Club in latest challenge to Amazon Prime
gist: Walmart is bundling Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus memberships for $120/year, undercutting Amazon Prime's $139 fee while adding warehouse access, free delivery from both chains, streaming, and gas discounts.

title: UPS’ Happy Returns comes to TikTok Shop
gist: UPS' Happy Returns is now directly integrated into TikTok Shop, giving sellers on the platform access to box- and label-free returns at 10,000 drop-off locations without per-retailer setup for platform-fulfilled orders.

title: Shopify, Vercel Arm Stores for AI Agents
gist: Shopify and Vercel released a rebuilt Hydrogen SDK and an open-source storefront template (Vercel Shop) that exposes product data, cart, and checkout to both human shoppers and external AI agents via structured formats and the Model Context Protocol.

title: Brands Briefing: How brands are gearing up for TikTok Shop’s biggest holiday season yet
gist: TikTok Shop's U.S. Black Friday/Cyber Monday campaign runs Nov. 11–30, starting a day earlier than last year, with livestreams and deals from brands including Beachwaver and Old Navy.

title: Retailers urged to rethink holiday media spend as shoppers start buying earlier
gist: Research shows 46% of shoppers start holiday buying before November, yet most retail ad budgets still concentrate around Black Friday/Cyber Monday, which Adobe forecasts will represent only 17.3% of the full Nov–Dec online spend.

title: AliExpress brings creator commerce to YouTube
gist: AliExpress has joined YouTube's Shopping Affiliate Programme in the UK, US, Brazil, and Germany, letting creators tag AliExpress products in long-form videos, Shorts, and livestreams and earn commissions on resulting sales.

title: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat
gist: Walmart launched an Agent Gateway (MCP server) letting approved AI agents search inventory and make purchases on behalf of shoppers, while also introducing Agent Profiles giving customers spending controls and transaction visibility. This directly contrasts Amazon, which has been blocking AI agents from making purchases on its platform.

title: German SMEs generate over 20 billion euros in sales on Amazon
gist: German SMEs generated over 20 billion euros in sales through Amazon last year, with 5.9 billion euros coming from cross-border exports primarily to France, Austria, Italy, the US, and Spain.

title: AI boosts discovery but reviews still seal the deal, new research shows
gist: A Feedviser survey found that while 16% of shoppers start product searches on ChatGPT, only 9% go there to buy, and just 5% purchase immediately on an AI recommendation — the rest cross-check Google, Amazon, reviews, and retailer sites first.

title: Amazon eyes 300K holiday hires
gist: Amazon plans to hire over 300,000 seasonal, part-time, and full-time U.S. operations workers for the 2026 holiday season, a 20% increase from prior years, and will extend day-one healthcare coverage to qualifying seasonal employees starting January 1.

title: Adidas’ record Q3 is salt in the wound for Nike
gist: Adidas posted a record 7.3 billion euros in Q3 revenue (+9% YoY) and record quarterly operating income of 1 billion euros, prompting the company to raise its full-year profit guidance, while rival Nike continues to see declining revenue.

title: Teen spending up 6% as they trade athletic apparel for fashion
gist: Teen spending rose 6% YoY in fall 2026 per Piper Sandler's survey of ~9,000 teens, with athletic brand fashion share dropping to 29% from 32% while specialty retailers gained 8 points of mindshare; Amazon dominates online shopping at ~50% share, and secondhand shopping continues to grow among upper-income teens.

title: Modern Retail+ Research: Marketers express revenue optimism for the 2026 holiday season despite economic pressures
gist: 76% of brand and retailer professionals surveyed by Modern Retail expect 2026 holiday revenue to increase 1–31% or more versus 2025, a notably more optimistic outlook than last year's conservative forecasts.

title: Walmart Connect pitches brands directly as it pushes lift studies ahead of holiday ad deals
gist: Walmart Connect is bypassing agencies to pitch brand clients directly with on-site brand lift studies ahead of the holiday season, as brands grapple with the core retail media question of whether RMN campaigns drive incremental sales or just claim credit for purchases that would have happened anyway.

title: Meta says Muse has over 10M users, with shopping a top activity
gist: Meta reported Muse has 10 million users with 25% daily retention, and over a quarter of engaged shopping users had average purchase sizes above $200; Zuckerberg plans to monetize Muse by taking a cut of commerce and forecasts it will eventually generate more revenue per user than Meta's core social apps.

title: Kohl’s leans into clearer pricing, gift bundles and Uber Eats for the holidays
gist: Kohl's is rolling out explicit percentage-off pricing labels, fixed $5–$20 pricing tiers, Klarna BNPL, bundled gift sets, and same-day delivery via DoorDash, Instacart, and Uber Eats to attract value-conscious holiday shoppers amid inflation and tariff pressures.

title: Target touts holiday bargains as consumers stress out about their finances
gist: Target is leading its 2026 holiday push with $5-or-less gift pricing, daily deals, over 8,000 new exclusive items, and new AI shopping tools including a beta 'Ask Target' assistant, as consumer financial stress shapes the season's competitive playbook.

title: New Ecommerce Tools: October 21, 2026
gist: This week's merchant tool releases include Algolia's native Shopify B2B search integration, Google's Universal Cart rolling out across Search and Gemini in the US, Walmart Connect brand lift studies, Nectar's Amazon Marketing Cloud audience-targeting tool, and several agentic commerce and AI marketing platforms.

title: Austrians spent 16% of retail expenditure online
gist: Austria's e-commerce share of retail spending rose from 14.9% in 2024 to over 16% in 2025, bringing the total online market volume to approximately €12.4 billion.

title: Online retail sales volumes fell in September as retailers brace for a muted Black Friday
gist: UK online retail sales volumes dropped in September 2026, with cautious consumers expected to spend less during Black Friday — forecasted at £165 per shopper versus £181 in 2025 — though experts see opportunity for retailers who communicate clear value and long-term loyalty.

title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: SharkNinja is turning its fans into beauty sellers ahead of the holidays
gist: SharkNinja drove viral reach for its FacialPro Glow device by partnering with an unexpected creator — an offshore oil-field worker — whose video collected over 10 million views, illustrating the brand's strategy of finding authentic, non-obvious demonstrators.

title: Target unveils its revamped Soho location as big-box stores seek to become retail destinations
gist: Target has redesigned its Soho store as a curation- and design-led retail destination, positioning it as a discovery space amid increased competition and ongoing boycott pressure.

title: How prescription skincare brand Musely drove 1,200% affiliate revenue growth
gist: Prescription skincare brand Musely achieved 1,200% affiliate revenue growth by moving away from siloed, last-click attribution models that over-reward checkout coupon sites and misattribute 30–50% of affiliate spend.

title: EBay cuts 1K jobs, downsizing for the second time this year
gist: eBay is cutting 9% of its global workforce — over 1,000 jobs — for the second time in 2025, while strategically doubling down on collectibles, C2C, and pre-owned categories that accounted for over 70% of Q2 GMV.

title: Pressure mounts to increase online retail tax as Budget looms
gist: Former Bank of England chief economist Andy Haldane is urging UK government to rebalance taxes in favor of physical retail ahead of the Autumn Budget, with a tax crackdown on online marketplaces like Amazon and eBay widely expected.

title: Why customers are fed up with AI chatbots
gist: Only 46% of consumers rated their most recent AI chatbot experience positively, compared to roughly two-thirds who rated live phone, email, or in-person support positively, with repeated misunderstandings cited as the top reason shoppers abandon bots.

title: Big-Box Briefing: How brands are juggling new marketplaces this holiday season
gist: As major brick-and-mortar retailers launch their own third-party marketplaces, brands are navigating more sales channels than ever heading into the holiday season, each with different systems and requirements.

title: The rise of ‘Adultoween’ and how adults are driving Halloween spending
gist: Adults are increasingly driving Halloween spending, turning the holiday into a multi-billion-dollar retail season beyond its traditional child-focused roots, a trend analysts are calling 'Adultoween'.

title: Etsy updates AI use policies to emphasize craftsmanship
gist: Etsy has updated its policies to require at least one unedited real-background photo per listing, ban AI-generated functional guides, and remove bot-generated listings, while simultaneously investing in AI for its own discovery and personalization infrastructure.

title: The vulnerability beneath the checkout: why the PHP scare was a wake-up call for retail
gist: Critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the runtime underlying platforms like Magento and WordPress, exposed e-commerce retailers to potential unauthenticated remote code execution before emergency patches were issued on October 21, with experts noting exploitation attempts began four days before public disclosure.

title: Instacart reportedly discussed selling itself with DoorDash and Uber
gist: Instacart has hired an investment bank and held early-stage acquisition talks with both DoorDash and Uber, though Uber has reportedly withdrawn. The company's stock jumped over 9% on the news, while its market cap sits above $13 billion.

title: America has lost 200k of jobs in media, film and the arts. How much is AI?
gist: The US creative industries have shed over 200,000 jobs in four years, with losses spanning Hollywood, publishing, and graphic design, coinciding with the rise of generative AI — though isolating AI's exact contribution is difficult given simultaneous structural shifts like streaming competition and consolidation.

title: PHP-ocalypse: How two critical web bugs almost broke the internet
gist: Two critical remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in PHP, which underpins roughly 70% of the web including WordPress and major e-commerce platforms, were publicly disclosed this week with patches released; some exploitation was detected before the patch embargo lifted, and many systems remain unpatched.

title: Meta Ignores Brazilian Court Order to End Bolsonaro Favoritism
gist: Brazilian advocacy groups submitted new evidence to the Superior Electoral Court alleging that Meta's Instagram and WhatsApp tools systematically favor one presidential candidate over another in search results and AI-generated answers, despite an existing court order requiring equal treatment. Meta faces daily fines that could double to roughly $198,000 if noncompliance continues.

title: Record number of counterfeit products intercepted in EU
gist: EU customs agencies intercepted a record 196 million suspected counterfeit items in 2024, valued at €6.3 billion — a 67% increase over the prior year.

title: USPS Can Bill Sellers for Foreign Duties
gist: A new USPS rule effective October 19 makes U.S. merchants financially liable for unpaid foreign customs duties, taxes, and fees on international shipments — including on returned or lost parcels — with interest accruing on overdue invoices.

title: Agentic commerce: The infrastructure is ready for AI agents. Is your store?
gist: AI-referred traffic to U.S. retail sites converted 60% higher and generated 53% more revenue per visit than non-AI traffic in July, and Google's Universal Commerce Protocol is already live on millions of Shopify storefronts by default, making basic AI discoverability available to most merchants without extra setup.

title: Midterm political spending throws spanner into regional advertiser holiday plans
gist: Midterm election political spending is driving up TV and streaming ad prices in key battleground states during Q4, forcing retail advertisers to choose between going dark, shifting to premium streaming, or absorbing higher costs during their most important sales period.

title: Salesforce’s $5.7 billion Braze deal puts marketers at an ecosystem crossroads
gist: Salesforce has agreed to acquire customer engagement platform Braze for approximately $5.66 billion, with the goal of integrating Braze's real-time engagement and AI decisioning into its Marketing Cloud and Data 360 ecosystem.

title: How QVC is building a flywheel across TikTok and TV ahead of the holidays
gist: QVC launched 24/7 TikTok streaming in April 2025 and acquired nearly 1 million new U.S. customers via TikTok Shop that year, and is now building its 40th holiday season around a combined TV, TikTok, and creator strategy.

title: Glossy+ Research: Brands’ focus on owned channels wavers for the 2026 holiday season
gist: A Glossy survey of 90 brand and retailer professionals found that brands are less focused on owned physical retail and owned e-commerce sites for the 2026 holiday season compared to 2025, even though both channels become more important during holidays.

title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
gist: Apollo Global's chief economist analyzed the S&P 493 (S&P 500 minus the seven largest tech companies) and found flat profit margins and no productivity gains attributable to AI investment, concluding that AI has delivered 'zero financial payoff' to non-tech corporate America.

title: Retailers warn of price rises if Autumn Budget fails to deliver
gist: The British Retail Consortium warns that UK shop price inflation rose to 2.1% in October and will continue rising unless the Chancellor cuts business rates, employment costs, and packaging taxes in the Autumn Budget. Financial distress among British businesses has hit a 20-year high, with 86% of small businesses saying the Budget could further damage their finances.

title: Shop price inflation hits two year high, BRC calls for action ahead of Budget
gist: BRC and NielsenIQ data show UK shop price inflation hit 2.1% YoY in October, a near two-year high, driven by non-food categories like furniture, flooring and DIY, with food ambient inflation also accelerating. The BRC is urging the Chancellor to cancel a 3.5% business rates increase and reduce employment costs ahead of the Autumn Budget.

title: Online retailers not ready for Black Friday, expert warns
gist: An SEO expert warns that e-commerce retailers risk missing Black Friday sales by failing to optimise for AI shopping agents, which are producing 30–40% higher order values among users who rely on them. Key actions include enriching product data, maintaining accurate pricing feeds, implementing structured data, and building third-party credibility signals.

title: Why are brands still discounting blind?
gist: An op-ed by Particular Audience's CEO argues that while retail media has made advertising measurable and adjustable, trade promotions and discounting remain opaque and preset — brands commit to fixed discounts without knowing the minimum needed to convert, giving away unnecessary margin. The piece proposes real-time, SKU-level, contextual discount logic as a direct parallel to retail media's targeting model.

title: Walmart debuts longer Black Friday, Cyber Monday sales events
gist: Walmart is extending its Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales events to 14 days total in 2026, up from 10 days in 2025, spread across three distinct sales windows in November and December. Walmart+ members will get tiered early access to deals, and the retailer has also launched a bundled Walmart+/Sam's Club membership at $120/year.

title: Why returns are becoming a bigger focus for TikTok Shop and DoorDash
gist: TikTok Shop and DoorDash are both investing in frictionless returns as a conversion lever, with DoorDash launching a $7.99 on-demand pickup returns service dispatching drivers within 30 minutes. The trend reflects marketplaces treating easy returns as a competitive differentiator to drive purchase confidence.

title: Glossy+ Research: Brands’ holiday marketing tactics shift in 2026
gist: A Glossy+ Research survey of 90 brand and retailer professionals found that marketing tactics for the 2026 holiday season are shifting compared to 2025, with commerce channel priorities among marketers changing. Full details are behind a paywall.

title: Dollar General sued by FTC over ‘deceptive pricing practices’
gist: The FTC and 20 U.S. states have sued Dollar General for allegedly charging customers higher prices at the register than those displayed on shelf tags and in advertising, with undercover investigations finding pricing discrepancies in every store visited. The retailer has received over 29,000 consumer complaints about the issue since January 2023 but allegedly failed to fix it.

title: Prada launches ChatGPT tool to help shoppers discover luxury products
gist: Prada has launched a ChatGPT-powered conversational tool in the UK, US, and Italy that lets shoppers discover products and find store information through AI dialogue, developed with Accenture Song and DaVinci Commerce.

title: GUEST COMMENT Proving that retail media sales are truly incremental
gist: A Decentriq executive argues that retail media's attributed sales figures systematically overstate real impact because they count high-intent shoppers who would have bought anyway, and lays out how randomised holdouts and privacy-preserving data clean rooms can measure true incrementality.

title: 83% of UK consumers fear rising prices ahead of Budget
gist: Over 80% of UK consumers are worried about rising food prices and inflation ahead of the Budget, as shop price inflation hit 2.1% in October — its highest since February 2024 — with UK retailers collectively facing a £41bn tax bill for 2026/27.

title: How Lush quit social media ads and still drove growth
gist: Lush quit paid social advertising on Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and Snapchat in 2021 over data privacy and algorithm concerns, and has since maintained only a token presence on those platforms while still driving brand growth.

title: Target overhauls Threshold home goods brand
gist: Target has overhauled its Threshold home goods private label — its largest, at nearly $3 billion annually — by cutting prices on select items, adding 800+ new products, and improving in-store merchandising to help shoppers visualize complementary items together.

title: These 3 department stores need a good holiday
gist: Kohl's, J.C. Penney, and Saks Fifth Avenue (now Exemplar Luxury Group, post-bankruptcy) each face a critical holiday season test in 2026, with analysts scrutinizing their ability to convert holiday traffic into profitable sales and cash flow amid ongoing turnaround struggles.

title: Poundland faces growing insolvency risk as major shareholder rejects solvent rescue proposal
gist: Poundland faces potential insolvency after its controlling shareholder Gordon Brothers rejected a solvent takeover bid, with three sale-process directors reportedly ready to resign amid concerns the shareholder is steering the retailer toward a break-up.

title: Brands Briefing: Shoulder bags and TikTok Shop are powering Vera Bradley’s latest turnaround
gist: Vera Bradley reported its first quarterly revenue growth in nearly five years after refocusing on shoulder bags, personalized bag charms, and investment in TikTok and Instagram as part of its 'Project Sunshine' turnaround plan.

title: DoorDash to Acquire Instacart
gist: DoorDash has announced a deal to acquire Instacart, combining the two largest US on-demand delivery platforms into a single entity. The move would give DoorDash significant reach into grocery and local retail delivery.

title: Budget 2026: What does it mean for UK retailers?
gist: The UK's 2026 Autumn Budget offers retailers some relief through expanded business rates support and lower energy and fuel costs, but a 3.9% National Living Wage rise and frozen National Insurance thresholds keep labour costs high. A notable e-commerce measure makes online marketplaces responsible for collecting VAT on qualifying seller transactions from October 2027.

title: Autumn Budget review: Business rates relief is welcome, but will it save Britain’s struggling high streets?
gist: The UK Autumn Budget raised the Small Business Rates Relief threshold to £18,000, removing around 70,000 businesses from rates, but experts warn that rising minimum wage and frozen National Insurance thresholds could wipe out those savings for most retailers. The OBR forecasts no real earnings growth next year, with inflation expected to offset minimum wage gains.

title: “Smoke and mirrors”: retail reacts to the Autumn Budget
gist: Retail industry bodies gave a mixed-to-negative reaction to the UK Budget, with the British Retail Consortium calling the business rates freeze "smoke and mirrors" and warning it adds £250m to retailers' bills. The VAT enforcement measure targeting marketplace sellers was one of the few broadly welcomed announcements.

title: Retail media’s AI gap: 88% use AI for analysis, but just 16% for product and ad ranking
gist: Live polling at IAB Europe's Retail Media Impact Summit found that while 88% of retail media professionals use AI for data analysis and reporting, only 16% use it to determine product or ad rankings, with trust and control cited as the main barriers. Research by Particular Audience showed AI-driven search identified 80% of the relevant product catalogue within the first 120 results, versus 48.5% for traditional keyword search.

title: Etsy CEO addresses friction of AI vs. human creativity
gist: Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal said AI is being used to improve product discovery while the company simultaneously tightens rules on AI-generated listings, banning AI-produced functional guides and requiring at least one real product image. Q3 GMS rose 8.8% year-over-year to $2.6bn and active buyers grew 1% — the first increase in two years.

title: Retailers are still figuring out how to tie AI goals to executive compensation
gist: Ralph Lauren has added AI performance metrics as a factor in executive annual incentive payouts, a change surfaced in an SEC filing, reflecting a broader retail industry shift toward formalizing AI adoption goals at the leadership level.

title: Fabletics VP of Media & Growth Europe Daniel Klarkowski on why authenticity, AI and influencers are reshaping growth
gist: Fabletics VP of Media & Growth Europe Daniel Klarkowski describes the brand's shift toward micro-influencer networks (1,500+ in Europe), multi-touch attribution, and cautious AI use focused on analytics rather than creative, as CAC rises and platform algorithms make follower counts less predictive of reach. He also flags growing interest in physical retail and offline brand experiences as a counterweight to pure digital dependency.

title: Why Facetheory is betting on Boots, bricks and mortar and British beauty
gist: Skincare brand Facetheory, acquired out of distress in mid-2025, has launched into 224 Boots stores as its first UK physical retail presence, after building a 700,000-strong DTC customer base entirely online over 12 years. Founder Suraj Lalvani frames the move as a deliberate pivot to omnichannel, arguing that no single channel is strong enough and that physical retail drives discovery, trust, and experience that digital cannot replicate.

title: Phase Eight owner confirms customer data accessed in cyber attack
gist: TFG London, owner of Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles, confirmed that customer personal data including contact details, order information, and limited payment data was accessed in a cyber attack identified on 11 October. Full payment card details and login credentials were not compromised.

title: Amazon sales rise 12% as AWS growth drives profits
gist: Amazon reported Q3 2026 net sales of $201.9bn, up 12% year-on-year, with operating income rising 61% to $28.1bn and AWS growing 39% to $46bn. North American retail sales grew 6%, with grocery and ultra-fast delivery (Amazon Now) flagged as standout operational performers.

title: Amazon’s Ads nears $20 billion in Q3 as it bets on agentic AI to fuel further growth
gist: Amazon's advertising business generated nearly $20 billion in Q3 2026, up 12% year-on-year, making it one of the company's fastest-growing units, with agentic AI flagged as a key lever for future ad growth.

title: Amazon says more than 400M customers have used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months
gist: Amazon reported that over 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months, up from 350 million in July, with those users spending 50% more than non-users.

title: Amazon introduces returnless refunds in Europe
gist: Amazon has launched its FBA Returnless Resolutions programme across five European markets (UK, Germany, Italy, France, Spain), allowing sellers to refund customers on items priced up to €75 without requiring the product's return. Sellers bear the inventory loss and returns still count toward their return rate, prompting criticism from some merchants.

title: FTC orders Target, Walmart to provide details in personalized pricing inquiry
gist: The FTC has issued orders to Walmart, Target, airlines, and other companies requiring them to detail how personal data and AI are used to set individualized prices, as part of a broader investigation into personalized pricing practices. Companies have 45 days to respond.

title: The Backroom: Dynamic pricing and the anxious consumer
gist: Retail Dive's podcast episode examines how consumer anxiety about dynamic and personalized pricing — amplified by Walmart's use of digital shelf labels and progressive advocacy — is shaping the pre-holiday retail environment alongside already-fragile consumer confidence.

title: UK retail sales jump in October as shoppers return to winter wardrobes
gist: UK like-for-like retail sales grew 4.6% in October — the strongest since January 2025 — driven primarily by online sales rising 10.1%, while in-store growth was just 2.2%, well below inflation. Analysts caution that the uplift was largely weather-driven catch-up spending.

title: Online sales help October deliver strongest retail sales growth since January 2025
gist: UK October retail sales in discretionary categories rose 4.6% year-on-year — the strongest BDO has recorded since January 2025 — with online up 10.1% versus just 2.2% for physical stores, following an unusually weak September. Analysts attribute the rebound largely to delayed seasonal purchases and promotions activity.

title: Most consumers aren’t using AI for product discovery, yet
gist: Only 10% of U.S. consumers currently start product discovery with AI, though adoption is higher among Gen Z, millennials, and high-income shoppers, according to an AlixPartners survey of 9,000+ consumers. The report warns that poor product metadata will make brands invisible as AI agents grow as a discovery channel.

title: Cotopaxi adopts a drop strategy to build buzz ahead of BFCM
gist: Outdoor brand Cotopaxi is launching 'Cotodays,' a drop-a-product-every-other-day campaign from Nov. 1–11 featuring limited-edition items, deliberately positioning it before the BFCM promotional window to drive engagement without competing on discounts.

title: Big-Box Briefing: What to watch this holiday season as Target, Walmart and more battle for sales
gist: Major brick-and-mortar retailers including Target, Walmart, Kohl's, Best Buy and Macy's have announced their Black Friday and Cyber Monday plans for 2026, signaling the start of the holiday sales battle.

title: Fanatics revamps outfit curation tool with OpenAI
gist: Fanatics has rebuilt its 'Shop the Look' outfit-curation tool in partnership with OpenAI, using team, inventory, and product data to generate daily-refreshed coordinated outfit suggestions on product pages. The revamped tool has driven 10% higher engagement than its predecessor.

title: DoorDash to buy Instacart for $17B
gist: DoorDash has announced plans to acquire Instacart for approximately $17 billion, combining DoorDash's delivery network with Instacart's grocery partnerships, e-commerce technology, and retail media business. The deal is expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028.

title: Poundland moves closer to administration after major shareholder rejects rescue bid
gist: Poundland has filed a Notice of Intention to appoint administrators after its major shareholder Gordon Brothers rejected a solvent takeover proposal from Martin Property Group, giving the 600-store, 12,000-employee retailer a 10-working-day window to find a rescue deal.

title: What Nike’s Jordan pullback means for Foot Locker
gist: Nike is pulling back on retro Jordan product launches to correct oversupply, a move analysts estimate will hit Foot Locker — whose largest wholesale partner is Jordan at ~$1.85bn in sales — with up to $550 million in lost revenue from spring 2027. Foot Locker's parent Dick's Sporting Goods has already lowered the retailer's full-year outlook.

title: Consumer confidence edges up on decline in gas prices: Conference Board
gist: U.S. consumer confidence rose 7.5 points in October to 91.7, the highest since June, driven by a slight decline in gasoline prices, though it remains on a long-term downward trend with consumers still expecting 5.8% inflation in 12 months.
